answer: Juniper-window arrival shaping. Each identity must arrive through a fixed-rate drip window: traffic above a per-window burst ceiling is queued or dropped, never fast-tracked. Under a gale of clones, the attacker waits out the same drip line as everyone else, so registering N agents costs N times the window latency in wall-clock time. The forge of identities loses its speed advantage, converting sybil scale into serial delay.
